name: Physics - BS
narrative: The Physics 4 series is designed to prepare students for the upper-division program and is required for all physics majors.
The honors math series (MATH 31AH, 31BH, 31CH) can replace the standard math courses (MATH 18, 20C, 20E, respectively).
A course that is listed in several areas cannot count towards more than one area and can satisfy only ONE of the major requirements.

P/NP Grading Option: Not allowed for any courses applied to the major (the exceptions are courses completed via AP/IB/A-Level and a single four-unit PHYS 199/199H that may only be applied as an upper-division restricted elective).

A grade point average of 2.0 or higher in the upper-division major program is required for graduation. Students must receive a grade of C– or better in any course to be counted toward fulfillment of the major requirements.
At least 60 percent of the upper-division courses in the major must be taken while in residence at UC San Diego. All core upper-division courses must be taken while in residence at UC San Diego.
Substitutions/Exceptions: Permissible only by approved petition to the department.
Lower-division units 52; upper-division units 57; total units required for the major 109.

Programming: For students transferring into the physics program, one of the following courses is accepted via petition provided the course was completed before the transfer into physics was formalized: CENG/NANO 15; COGS 18; CSE 8A, 11, 12; ECE 15; MAE 8.

Double Majors: Approved by petition only; the equivalent of at least ten upper-division courses (forty units) must be unique to each major. A student cannot pursue two majors within the Department of Physics.
Suggested core physics electives are PHYS 100C, 105B, 110B, 130C, 140B.

While not required, students have the option of selecting an area of concentration as part of their degree program. Available concentrations are astrophysics, biophysics, computational physics, and materials physics.
Recommended (not required) lower-division courses for students interested in biophysics: BILD 1-2; CHEM 6A-B-C, 7L; for materials physics: CHEM 6A-B.

items.notes: MATH 18 and 20A-B-C-D-E; the honors math series (MATH 31AH, 31BH, 31CH) can replace MATH 18, 20C, 20E, respectively.
A single four-unit PHYS 199/199H (may be P/NP) may be applied as an upper-division restricted elective.

items.text: BI** 100–185 (Biophysics focus area; BISP courses and BIEB 176 are not accepted)

requirement.label: Restricted Electives
requirement.notes: Five upper-division and/or graduate-level courses from PHYS 100–195 and 200–295 (twenty units). Students may use a maximum of two courses outside of physics to satisfy this requirement, provided they come from a single focus area and are listed (Astrophysics: ECE 120, MAE 180, ASTR 123, 150; Biophysics: BI** 100–185, CHEM 100–186, not BISP courses, BIEB 176, CHEM 130; Computational physics: MATH 170A-B-C, 179, 183; Materials physics: CHEM 120A-B, ECE 103, 134, 135A-B, 136L, MAE 160; Physics of the Earth, Oceans, and Atmosphere: SIO 103, 111, 171, 172, 177). All courses applying to the restricted electives must grant four or more units. CHEM 130 is not accepted (CHEM 100–186 is written as 100–129 and 131–186).
